title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (December 2026) — the only 2026 edition that lands on an FOMC day-1, inside the confirmed Fed blackout
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php, re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 54,906 bytes) by this event's own initial research — its table lists "12/08/2026" for the December 2026 edition with a blank Notes cell, and states the release window as 12:00-12:15 pm ET. Doubly derived from the same page's stated rule ("the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", with the footnote that a Federal holiday on the preceding Monday pushes the release to Wednesday): 2026-12-03 is a Thursday, the following Tuesday is 12-08, and 12-07 is not a Federal holiday, so no adjustment applies. Filed estimate on two counts, neither of them date doubt: this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA (the standing schema gap eia-steo-2026-09-09 named), and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: Canonical entry written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-08), promoting the sole prior proposal eia-steo-2026-12-08.from-eia-steo-2026-10-06.json. Two of that proposal's framings are SHARPENED here rather than carried. (1) The appropriations exposure is real but lands DOWNSTREAM, not on this edition: PL 119-103 section 106 funds agencies through 2026-12-11, so 12-08 sits three days INSIDE the funded window and no lapse can reach it; the first STEO after the cliff is the January 2027 edition, 01/12/2027, proposed in this PR as eia-steo-2027-01-12.from-eia-steo-2026-12-08.json. (2) The 'Winter Fuels' framing the October sibling attached to 11-10 was already corrected by the November sibling on the same day (the WFO is an OCTOBER product on four EIA primaries) — not re-litigated here. WHAT IS NEW THIS SESSION, and the reason this edition is not the sibling's null repeated. FIRST, 2026-12-08 is FOMC day-1 of the Dec 8-9 SEP meeting (FED: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-08 — the asterisk is on the December row) and sits inside the confirmed Fed communications blackout 2026-11-28 -> 2026-12-10 that fomc-2026-12-09 already carries. Only 2 of the 20 STEO releases in the two-year sample landed on an FOMC day-1 (2025-05-06 and 2025-12-09), so the inherited 'STEO day is ordinary' null was measured almost entirely off this corridor and does not transfer to it unexamined. SECOND, the sample was doubled from n=8 to n=20 using EIA's own 2025 release-schedule table (archived snapshot, web.archive.org 2025-12-01), and that REFUTES two inherited quantitative claims as 2026-window artifacts: the October sibling's 'STEO days are ~2x more violent in crude' (CL=F full-day median 2.77% on the 2026-only n=8 — reproduced here to the cent, so the difference is sample and not method — against 1.15% in 2025 and 1.34% pooled versus 1.46% on all days: NO elevation), and its 'NG=F is markedly calmer on STEO days' (0.85% 2026-only, 2.31% 2025-only, 2.10% pooled vs 2.42% all days). THIRD, the FOMC day-1 base rate itself, measured over 16 meetings: crude full-day roughly doubles (CL=F 2.41% vs 1.46%, BZ=F 2.33% vs 1.35%, USO 2.67% vs 1.42%) while the 12:00-13:00 ET hour is the QUIETEST equity hour in the sample (NVDA 0.14% vs 0.30%, MSFT 0.12% vs 0.19%, SPY 0.08% vs 0.12%) — the pre-decision freeze. The exact structural precedent, 2025-12-09 (December edition, FOMC day-1, SEP meeting), reads near-silent in that hour: NVDA 0.02%, MRVL 0.03%, SPY 0.06%, CL=F 0.10%. Filed `low` on the sibling entries' reasoning, and the corridor reinforces rather than raises it: a noon forecast publication one day before an SEP decision and two days before CPI owns none of the day's attention. Kept on the board because it remains the scoreboard for the ERCOT/national load line under docs/research/ai-energy-constraint.md — Texas 2027 load growth cut 14% -> 6% in the August edition, national 2027 consumption 4,391 bkWh — which the ercot-data-center-audit-filing-2026-12-10 entry adjudicates two days later.
